narrative: OMX30 opens with tailwind from broad European and US equity rallies (+1-3%), supported by +1.1% correlation signal. Commodities surge (oil +2.95%, gold +1.29%) traditionally pressures industrials via input costs but may reflect global risk appetite. The index sits +5.4% above 200-MA in established bull, but Stochastic K=94.1/D=90.9 signals overbought conditions with RSI neutral at 55.6—classic setup for intraday pullback before continuation. Weak ADX (12.8) dampens conviction; yields down 117bp (10Y to 4.89%) removes near-term tailwind for banks. Watch 3180 resistance (50-MA) and 3085 support (lower Bollinger) for mean-reversion trades.
morningBrief: OMX30 set to open +0.7 to +0.9% on sustained risk appetite from US/EU overnight. Stochastic is deeply overbought (K=94, D=91)—expect profit-taking into resistance at 3180 (50-MA) but don't chase shorts; 200-MA at 3085 remains solid floor in bull regime. Brent crude +2.95% will pressure Volvo/Atlas Copco margin outlooks (higher logistics input costs), but USD/SEK bid (+0.14%) helps export pricing power. Boliden deserves top-of-list status: gold +1.29% and copper +0.17% = direct revenue upside; watch for sector rotation into cyclicals if tech sentiment holds. Banks face headwind from 117bp drop in 10Y yield—NIM compression risk for SEB, Handelsbanken despite overall bull tone. Key data: US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET (risk event if above 270k). Bias remains long for day-traders targeting 3180, but tighten stops at 3140 given overbought technicals and weak ADX.
